| Quality & Testing |  |
| **Goal:** To demonstrate that the milestone not only functions but is also high-quality, stable, and ready for use. **How to formulate an answer: Describe the QA process:** The QA process raised some governance concerns regarding ownership of the means of publishing as well as the means by which the evaluation process is enforced. There may be some latent opportunity for more open and transparent collective learning and evolution with regards to publishing and process design. 5 rounds of changes were requested by the evaluator to ensure the deliverables meet the expected presentation standard. All deliverables now successfully pass all requiurements. The process of adapting the presentation in order to conform to third-party requirements lasted longer than expected. **Detail quality standards:** Explain how high quality was ensured in key areas. For each area, describe the actions taken: **Performance:** The process was slower than expected and has had a material effect on the project’s viability, since market conditions are currently especially unforgiving. In the future, the capacity shortage created by holiday periods could be factored ahead of time to ensure dependent workstreams are not blocked.  **Security:** The extent to which the archive is anchored on-chain remains unclear. **Usability & Design:** Significant room for improvement was identified regarding the milestone submission and evalation process, which has been communicated to the committee.  **Link to Proof:** [https\://github.com/IntersectMBO/product-website/pull/64](https://github.com/IntersectMBO/product-website/pull/64) |  |
| Public Communication Summary |  |
| **Your Goal:** To write a clear, engaging summary of achievement that can be easily understood by a non-technical audience, such as community members or stakeholders. **How to formulate an answer (Tell a story by answering these questions): WHY.** The purpose of this project is to generate market entry playbooks to drive adoption of Cardano in emerging markets (LATAM and Africa). This milestone finalises initial commitments and confirms alignment between funded proposer and product committee, via a number of documents (milestone 1 deliverables). **WHERE.** This is important because the playbooks are locally-sourced. Spanning multiple regions and enabling local actors to publish the playbooks themselves, the project, once underway, must be able to navigate a high level of complexity without getting stuck in unnecessary explanations part-way through. Slow is smooth; smooth is fast. This milestone therefore aimed to create ample time for all parties to understand how best to steward the rest of the project as it unfolds. For those not familiar with working on living systems, this time for initial alignment and understanding was key. **WHAT.** Information and understanding was developed via an interactive, multi-media and highly networked repository of documentation. Key counterparties \- those we expect to collaborate with in due course \- were engaged ahead of time to introduce a shared intention as early as possible. Graphics were used to create visuals to aid with internalising the system complexity, creating a shared language form in complement to text. The space was prepared for training materials, as part of ensuring local actors are able to learn what is needed for them to be fully unlocked to contribute effectively, from their full agency. Practically, this meant translating from the what of the proposal to the how of organising with local actors. **SO WHAT.** Like many blockchains, Cardano continues to face challenges in real-world adoption. There is a gap between the projection of what new capabilities its technology could create and the realities of everyday people, businesses and individuals alike. This project affirms there is no one that better understands those realities than the people themselves, and it enables them to author their own adoption pathways: their narratives, their language, their needs and opportunities. That’s what locally-sourced market entry playbooks means. We’re also not stopping there. Leveraging a recently completed technical build (thanks to Catalyst for funding) we’re planning to use verifiable claims (VCs) to add an additional layer of security to the playbooks, giving the client, Cardano Product Committee, the assurance they need to action the insights published. This is a highly ambitious scope, given the budget and current ADA price, but we want to see these playbooks being used to direct resources to local actors that can embed Cardano at the heart of existing organisations playing a key role in their region. In that way, we hope to see meaningful steps being taken to connect emerging realities with relevant Cardano adoption to create real-world value beyond the Cardano ecosystem itself. **WHAT’S NEXT.** This project’s own documentation lives at docs.prisma.events/events/cpc. Visit prisma.events to learn more.  |  |
